chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on the Day of Arafaat at the Mawqif, and he was calling out in a loud voice: 'O people! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was the Imam, then Ali ibn Abi Talib, then al-Hasan, then al-Husayn, then Ali ibn al-Husayn, then Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), then Hah!' So he called out three times to those in front of him, and on his right, and on his left, and behind him, making twelve calls in total.
And Amr said: 'So when I went to Mina, I asked the masters of Arabic about the interpretation of
So they said: 'Hah' in the language of the clan of so-and-so means 'I', so ask me.' He said: 'Then I asked others as well from the masters of Arabic, and they said the same.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve Imams mentioned by Imam al-Sadiq at Mawqif?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the Imam's public declaration of the Twelve Imams' succession during the pivotal Day of Arafaat, a time of spiritual convergence for pilgrims. The use of the dialectal term 'Hah' for 'I' serves as a linguistic marker for the twelfth Imam, emphasizing the continuity of divine authority (Imamah) from the Prophet through the Ahl al-Bayt. This narration underscores the Shia belief in the explicit designation (Nass) of each Imam by his predecessor, reinforcing the theological legitimacy of the Imams' leadership.
